task_spec:
> Using the Global Weather Repository CSV, produce:
> 1. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest cities**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 2. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest countries**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 3. **Print the top 10 lists to the console** before plotting: for each of the 4 charts, print the ranked names and their temperature values (e.g., "1. Paris: 25.2 deg C")
> 4. A **100-word summary** for a non-technical audience explaining the rankings and any notable patterns
>
> Column reference: cities are in `location_name`, countries in `country`, temperature in `temperature_celsius`.

report_draft: The world's hottest cities and countries reveal a striking geographic pattern. By average temperature, the Middle East and North Africa dominate: Ar Riyadh (45.0°C) and Kuwait (44.4°C) top the cities list, while Saudi Arabia, Morocco, and Turkmenistan lead countries. However, single hottest measurements tell a different story. Suva, Fiji recorded a dramatic 79.3°C—far exceeding its typical average—suggesting an extreme heat event. Middle Eastern cities like Kuwait City (49.2°C) and Baghdad (49.1°C) show more consistent extremes. Overall, the data illustrates how consistent, year-round heat (Middle East) differs from rare, intense spikes (tropical regions), revealing two distinct patterns of extreme temperature.
